routes.description: Establish a cumulative inference from cosmic order and fine-tuning, moral and aesthetic experience, resurrection testimony, and personal revelation to a purposeful, relational God specifically identified with Christianity.
routes.successCriteria: The combined considerations must be more expected or intelligible under Christian theism than under skeptical agnosticism, must bridge from a generic intelligence to the Christian God, and must remain evidentially weighty after objections from suffering, rival explanations, historical development, and naturalistic mechanisms.

motionBridge.description: Show that the named scientific, moral, historical, revelatory, and aesthetic considerations cumulatively make Christian theism more plausible than withholding belief through skeptical agnosticism.

centralBridges.description: Connect the universe's beginning, lawful mathematical order, and life-permitting constants to purposeful intelligence while explaining why rival naturalistic or creator hypotheses do not absorb the inference equally well.
Connect objective moral orientation, radical altruism, beauty, and relational purpose to a personal and good God rather than stopping at an unspecified designer.

Establish that the historical case concerning Jesus, crucifixion, empty-tomb traditions, appearances, and early witness supports resurrection strongly enough to identify the inferred God with Christianity.

Explain why evolutionary suffering, natural evil, contested scripture, source-development concerns, and natural mechanisms for religious or aesthetic experience do not overturn the cumulative inference.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify committed belief through converging noncoercive evidence without requiring mathematical proof or certainty.
Explain how personal revelation and evolved capacities for numinous experience can supply additional evidence without substituting private experience for the public cumulative case.

routes.description: Defend skeptical agnosticism by testing whether the proposed considerations distinctly favor coherent Christian theism, comparing them with rival explanations and counterevidence, and preserving uncertainty where the available inferences remain underdetermined.
routes.successCriteria: Show that the cumulative case does not warrant the claimed comparative preference because its observations are insufficiently specific to Christianity, face credible naturalistic or rival-theistic explanations, and are offset by suffering, scriptural tension, historical uncertainty, and limits on public access to private revelation.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning, morality, resurrection, revelation, and beauty do not cumulatively establish Christian theism as more plausible than skeptical agnosticism.

centralBridges.description: Require an intelligible and sufficiently specific account of the Christian God so that the observations can be tested against that hypothesis rather than an undefined creator or contested revelation.

Compare fine-tuning with divine omnipotence, rival creator hypotheses, cosmic waste, and evolutionary suffering to determine whether the total natural evidence is more expected under a loving creator than under mindless development.
Test resurrection claims through source dependence, genre, theological development, multiple attestation, visionary alternatives, and the uncertain traditions concerning witnesses and martyrdom.

Determine whether moral intuition, scripture, personal revelation, and aesthetic experience coherently and publicly identify Christianity rather than supporting only private justification or ambiguous transcendence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Apply uncertainty symmetrically so that unknown divine purposes cannot answer counterevidence while unknown natural explanations are excluded from affirmative evidence.
Distinguish the importance of investigating Christianity from the stronger burden of holding that its truth is comparatively established.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Cosmic Order, and the Creator Hypothesis
sections.rationale: Covers the inference from cosmic beginnings, lawful mathematical order, and life-permitting constants to intelligence, together with disputes about omnipotence, physical constraint, multiverse alternatives, and rival creator hypotheses.

sections.title: Evolutionary Suffering, Natural Evil, and Divine Purpose
sections.rationale: Covers whether lawful evolution and the emergence of relational creatures reconcile suffering with a loving creator, or whether the scale and avoidability of animal suffering favor mindless natural development.

sections.title: Morality, Altruism, and Scriptural Coherence
sections.rationale: Covers the proposed movement from objective moral orientation and radical altruism to a personal good God, alongside challenges concerning natural explanation and tensions between moral intuition and Christian scripture.

sections.title: Resurrection and the Historical Identification of Christianity
sections.rationale: Covers whether crucifixion, empty-tomb traditions, appearances, early testimony, and witness traditions establish resurrection, considering source dependence, genre, theological development, visionary alternatives, and martyrdom uncertainty.

sections.title: Personal Revelation, Beauty, and Public Accessibility
sections.rationale: Covers whether prayer experiences, numinous encounters, music, and beauty provide additional evidence for Christian theism, including evolutionary mechanisms, alternative interpretations, private justification, and limits on public evidential access.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-04.proposition: The universe's beginning, life-permitting constants, and mathematically elegant laws collectively support an inference to an intelligence behind nature.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-05.proposition: Objective morality and radical altruism, which Collins argues evolutionary psychology does not fully explain, support moving beyond a deistic intelligence toward a personal, value-grounding God.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-08.proposition: The narrow life-permitting ranges of physical constants call for explanation, and Collins regards an intelligent creator and uncaused cause as less faith-demanding than an unobservable multiverse.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Evolution is an elegant process consistent with a God of order, and its suffering need not imply blind randomness if the emergence of complex life was built into the plan from the beginning.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Natural harms accompany stable physical laws unless God continually intervenes, and Collins argues that God accepted this cost for the advent of creatures capable of relationship with God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Jesus's crucifixion, reports of the empty tomb and risen appearances, and witnesses who maintained their testimony collectively support resurrection despite its miraculous character.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Historical judgments about unique Gospel testimony are influenced by prior commitments, so occurrence in only one Gospel does not by itself make the testimony incredible.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Cosmic order, objective moral orientation, Jesus's teaching, and the resurrection cumulatively support Christian faith while recognition of human epistemic limits undercuts confident atheistic certainty.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: A specific and unwelcome message received during prayer can reasonably count as personal revelation when it seems unlike self-generated thought and produces lasting changes in priorities.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-03.proposition: Evolutionary or neural functions for musical perception do not eliminate its divine significance because evolved human capacities may mediate forms of revelation otherwise inaccessible to people.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-06.proposition: Claims that observations support God are difficult to test when God is said to exceed comprehension and meaningful descriptions depend on contested scriptural revelation.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-07.proposition: Christianity weakens its moral inference to God when biblical material conflicts with the same moral intuition offered as evidence for a good divine source.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-09.proposition: Fine-tuning may count against classical theism because an unconstrained creator should not require a thought-permitting universe balanced on a narrow range of physical constants.

chunk-001:chunk001-candidate-10.proposition: Fine-tuning does not uniquely identify the Christian God because the same material improbability can fit rival creator accounts, including an imperfect or malevolent demiurge.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Although fine-tuning offers some support to theism, cosmic lifelessness and immense evolutionary animal suffering are more expected under mindless natural development than under a loving creator.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: An unknown divine explanation for suffering licenses analogous uncertainty about a natural explanation for fine-tuning, while conceivable less-predatory ecosystems undermine the necessity of extreme animal suffering.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: The increasingly elaborate post-resurrection appearances in later Gospels are better explained as mythological development after Jesus's death than as progressively detailed history.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Uncertain traditions about the disciples' martyrdom and the visionary character of Paul's experience provide weaker resurrection evidence than established bodily eyewitness testimony would provide.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: A striking personal revelation could legitimately ground belief for its recipient, while philosophical argument alone may be ineffective and make divine access seem unfairly elitist.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-01.proposition: The painful and unsettled quality of aesthetic experience may register that reality falls short of how it ought to be rather than straightforwardly evidencing God.
